text:
Alex: heads-up — this morning we saw another hit on the us-west1-spot-gpu pool, ~25% slower node readiness and ~12 evictions across inference-prod. Pods were Pending for up to 4m. :grimacing:

Maria: yep saw alerts from node-exporter + autoscaler logs. looks like a churn wave around 03:14 UTC, probably AZ-level preemptions. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cluster/spot-gpu-us-west1 :eyes:

SRE-Bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaleDown forbidden: NodeGroup us-west1-spot-gpu is subject to recent preemptions, eviction threshold exceeded.

Jin: idea — instead of full reliance on big spot pool, we should keep a tiny warm-standby pool of 2-4 on-demand GPUs with a hard taint so only fallback jobs land. that reduces cold-start failures for critical inferences.

Lee: strongly +1 for warm standby. cost delta is small vs SLO misses. We can use taint: `node.kubernetes.io/standby=true:NoSchedule` and a toleration on a low-priority fallback nodeSelector in the API router.

Maria: also propose staggering drains during rolling node replacement. current draining is simultaneous across 6 nodes which spikes Pending. if we set `maxUnavailable: 1` on our rollout plus `scaleDownUtilizationThreshold` tweak, that should smooth it.

Alex: curious about CA config — can we make the cluster-autoscaler prefer diversifying instance types and AZs to avoid single-AZ waves? any config snippets?

Jin: yes — set multiple instance-groups and enable `balance-similar-node-groups` and `expander=least-waste`. also set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5` for GPUs. snippet we tested:```yaml
--nodes=2:10:us-west1-spot-gpu-a
--nodes=2:10:us-west1-spot-gpu-b
--balance-similar-node-groups
--expander=least-waste
```

Lee: we should add a health-check job that warms KV caches on standby nodes immediately after they join (small DaemonSet) — avoids long warmup for first serving request.

Ops: cost note — 4 on-demand gpus in warm pool is ~0.6x monthly reserve cost vs transient timeout penalties. happy to run numbers if we decide on size.

Maria: operational runbook idea: when CA sees >15% increase in pending pods and evictions in 10m, flip fallback-policy to `on-demand` and bump warm pool to 4. rollback after 30m stable. we can implement as an automation in infra-bot.

Alex: can someone draft the temp patch for terraform/nodepool and the autoscaler flags? i'll QA and schedule a canary in us-west1-alpha. target window tonight 0200-0400 UTC. :thumbsup:

Jin: will create PR with: 1) node-pool terraform for `gpu-warm-standby` (min 2, max 4, on-demand, tainted) 2) CA arg updates 3) small DaemonSet for cache-warmup. I'll include rollout docs and cost calc.

Lee: test checklist: smoke deploy, stress test with 200 concurrent inference requests, verify no evictions, confirm request latency p50/p95 within baseline.

SRE-Bot: created ticket INFRA-2143: "us-west1 spot warm-standby & staggered drain playbook" — assigned to Jin, Ops.

Ops: noted. i'll run quick cost delta and add the alarm that triggers warmup automation. planning to tag PR with `needs-rollback-plan`.

Alex: perfect. if we can get this out as a small canary and measure, should cut incident rate during AZ spot waves. thanks team.
